note: How the VIP Design System realizes the abstract language in ../../../patterns/index.json. Entries are keyed by `pattern` — an abstract id (`confirm`), a variant (`disclose.accordion`) or a part (`browse-collection#items`) — and every field means what docs/patterns-v2.md says it means. The reach-for table in patterns.md is generated from this file and the abstract one: run `npm run patterns-doc` in engine/ after editing either. Namespaced parts are written as the code writes them (`Dropdown.Item`, `Accordion.Root`); `canonical` is always the name the file imports (`Dropdown`, `Accordion`). **Anatomy entries** record a shape the library requires — a `Table` is rows of cells in every file that has one — and carry `canonical` set to the root import, so they keep `patterns/unregistered-composite` quiet about mandatory structure and never produce a finding of their own. **Judgement entries** record a composite with a right and a wrong form. `NewDialog.Root` and `Drawer` take their regions as props (`trigger`, `title`, `description`, `content`), which a signature does not see, so neither has an anatomy entry. Entries with no `canonical` are shapes the package does not ship: the first project to need one extracts it and fills `canonical` in. Seeded from composites that already recur in a real VIP Design System codebase (2026-09-24).

modal.note: NewDialog.Root takes its trigger, title, description and content as props, so it has no anatomy entry. A destructive confirmation is NewConfirmationDialog — see confirm.

drawer.note: Its regions are props too, so it has no anatomy entry.

instead_of: Rebuilding the row per form, with the label/toggle/description wiring re-typed each time
realizations.note: Not shipped. The field that recurs here is a setting switched on and off in place: a Label and a Toggle on one row, with help text under them. The Label's `htmlFor` names the Toggle's `id`, and the help text's `id` is the Toggle's `aria-describedby`. `ToggleRow` is a different shape — a list row with a `Heading` title, an optional image and badge, and no `<label>` association — so it is not a drop-in for this. Projects assemble this row by hand; the first one extracted becomes `canonical`, and the rest import it.

instead_of: The second Button carrying sx={{ ml: 2 }}
realizations.note: Two or three actions together: a `Flex` with `sx={{ gap: 2 }}`, primary last. Documentation, not a check — `Flex(Button, Button)` is under the four-node floor.
Commands on a thing. The trigger is `Dropdown.Root`'s `trigger` prop; the items are its children.

instead_of: A NewDialog.Root whose content is a message and a Cancel/Confirm Button pair — NewConfirmationDialog already is that, with the button order and focus handling fixed
realizations.note: Asking the user to confirm an action before it happens: any destructive or irreversible action, and any action that needs a second look. `trigger`, `title`, `description`, `label` for the confirm button, `buttonVariant`, `onConfirm`. The anti-shape is prose rather than an `instead_of_signature`: `NewDialog.Root` carries its content as a prop, so the Cancel/Confirm pair never appears as its JSX child, and a form dialog also ends in two buttons.

instead_of: A Card of Heading + Text + an arrow icon
realizations.note: A list of things to open: one `OptionRow` per item.

Every table. Recorded so rows of cells are not reported as an unregistered composite — including a row component that renders `TableRow(TableCell, …)` without importing `Table` itself. The package ships the table, not a data view, so this is the items part and not browse-collection.list.
Several independently expandable sections. `Accordion.Trigger` and `Accordion.TriggerWithIcon` are two spellings of one part, so the signature names both.

instead_of: A Notice that removes itself on a timer
A Spinner rendered inside a Button's children while a flag is set — `{ loading && <Spinner size={ 14 } sx={ { mr: 2 } } /> }`
realizations.note: A button whose action is in flight: `<Button loading>` — or `ButtonSubmit` for a form's submit — which draws the spinner beside the label, disables the button and sets `aria-busy`. The anti-shape is the action row it usually sits in, because `Button(Spinner)` alone is under the four-node floor. No `canonical`: every file that builds it already imports `Button`, which would read as deliberate.

instead_of: A Card holding a Heading, a Badge and a Flex of Buttons
